defectsReproduced: knownPrefills — participant.email mapped to 200-00132 field 34i is absent from the boundary artifact. Reproduced from the bytes: the flattened appearance XObject at rect x395.69 y120.55 exists in both fixtures; in the boundary artifact it draws `<> Tj` at /Helvetica 11 Tf. Root cause located in the shared fitter: the descending ladder starts at min(maxFontSize, rect.height - 2) = 10.96 on this 12.96pt-high widget and steps by 0.5, ending at 6.46, so 6.0 — the minimum readable size the module declares — is never evaluated. The value needs 165.6pt at 6.0 in a 170.7pt box and fits with five points to spare.
feeAndWaiver — no fee amount and no established waiver route; the instructions said so themselves.
service — no recipient and no method stated.
repairsMade: fitTextToWidget takes a new evaluateDeclaredMinimumSize option that tries the declared minimum as a final rung. Opt-in, defaulting to the existing ladder so no family outside this repair can change on its next rebuild. Characterised over 7,380 rect/value/multiline combinations: 41 outcomes change and every one is a refusal becoming a write at exactly 6.0pt; no value that already fits changes in any way.
The VT shared host opts in. The boundary email is now read back from the artifact's own bytes at 395.69,120.55 on packet page 3.

The byte proof now lists every mapped write the artifact does not carry, with the finalizer's reason, and the build ASSERTS that list is empty. The old build recorded the refusal only inside the finalizer's report, so the family's actual-writes.json claimed 8 values for a document holding 7 and the loss was invisible downstream.

feeAndWaiver and service are quoted from the Vermont Judiciary's own filing instructions, form 200-00130A (07/2025), held in the committed corpus: filing is free except a $90 fee to seal a conviction for a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a), waivable on the Application to Waive Filing Fees — which is 600-00228, already in this packet and filled; and the court, not the participant, provides the copy to the prosecutor who brought the criminal case once the petition is filed. Whether a given conviction falls under § 1201(a) is a docket fact and is delegated to the clerk rather than decided here.
